sections.h2: Selling a house in St. George
sections.html:
Utah's southwest corner, right at the Arizona line, is home to St. George, the Washington County seat. The city lies along Interstate 15 at 2,530 feet, roughly 118 miles northeast of Las Vegas and 300 miles south-southwest of Salt Lake City. Zion National Park is to the east and Snow Canyon State Park is close to town.

Residents numbered 49,728 in 2000 and 95,342 in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 108,713. About 13,000 people arrived in five years, which is why so many houses are newer. Retirees are a big part of the picture too, with 21.8% of residents age 65 or older, so downsizers and heirs selling an inherited house are common.

Housing and income rows cover 2020 to 2024. About two in three homes are owner-occupied. Read the median value as a survey number, not an offer on your house.

Buyers here check the heat defenses first. Monthly averages climb from 42.1 degrees in December to 87.8 degrees in July, and around 60 afternoons a year hit 100 degrees or more. The all-time high was 118 degrees on July 4, 2007.

Yearly precipitation is only about 9 inches, with 1.4 inches of snow on average. Even so, close to 60 mornings fall to freezing or colder, and pipes in a poorly insulated home can suffer.

  • Air conditioners and roofs wear fastest, so inspectors ask how old they are.
  • Stucco, window seals and flat roofs that have baked in the sun may hide damage you cannot see from the curb.
  • A house close to the Santa Clara River or a wash shares its flood history. The January 2005 flood destroyed 28 homes along the river, so drainage is a fair question.

Water is a live issue across the county. A 2022 ordinance from the regional water conservancy district bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial, institutional and industrial developments and limits grass at new homes.

Cities do the enforcing, from water-waste complaints to metering data and penalties. Heavy users have paid an added fee since 2023, and that revenue funds rebates for swapping grass for water-efficient landscaping. The district projected savings of nearly 11 billion gallons over ten years.

With a big lawn, check with the city or your water provider before paying for landscaping you hope will help the sale.

Named areas organize how buyers think about the city: Downtown, Bloomington, Entrada, Green Valley, Little Valley, Red Cliffs, Snow Canyon, Sunbrook, Sunriver, The Ledges, Tonaquint and Desert Hills. Each has its own character, so name yours in the listing.

  • Interstate 15 runs northeast to southwest through the city.
  • State Route 7, the Southern Parkway, runs east and west along the south edge, and SR-8, SR-34 and SR-18 also serve the city.
  • The regional airport in the southeast offers flights on American, Delta and United, all operated by SkyWest.
  • SunTran runs seven fixed bus routes.

High schools in the county school district include Desert Hills, Dixie, Pine View, Snow Canyon and Crimson Cliffs. Newcomers with children usually want to know which one an address feeds.

The county's property tax deadline is November 30, whether or not a notice reaches you. The tax attaches to the property rather than to its owner, so an unpaid bill follows the house to a new owner.

Late payment is delinquent under Utah Code section 59-2-1331, with a 2.5% penalty or $10, whichever is greater. Settling everything by January 31 reduces it to 1%. The treasurer takes partial payments of $10 or more per parcel at any time, and each May the clerk-auditor sells properties delinquent for at least five years.

At closing the title company splits the bill, and the settlement statement shows what each side owes.

A primary residence earns a 45% exemption on up to one acre. Rental homes can qualify, but vacation homes and time-shares cannot, so a second home in St. George is taxed on its full value. The Washington County assessor can say how your parcel is classified.

  • Treasurer: 111 East Tabernacle St., St. George, (435) 301-7720.
  • Auditor: (435) 301-7220. Lose before the county Board of Equalization and you can go on to the Utah State Tax Commission using Form TC-194, filed with the auditor within 30 days of the decision.

An unpaid balance must be cleared at or before closing, and that is routine. The title company treats it as a payoff, deducts it from what you receive and passes clean title to the buyer. Phone the treasurer for today's figure and get it in writing so it lines up with the closing statement.

sections.h2: Closing day and what to bring
sections.html:
Once you accept an offer, a title company searches the ownership record, confirms the tax status and prepares a settlement statement. You sign the deed and closing papers, any mortgage is paid off from the proceeds and the deed is recorded with the county.

Bring a photo ID, the keys and any remotes or gate codes. If the house has a pool, a casita or an irrigation controller, write down how it works for the next owner. A short list like that is a courtesy buyers remember.

The problems we hear are practical: an air conditioner or roof on its last legs, a yard that is costly to water, an heir living out of state, or a house that is miserable to show in July.

Selling for cash avoids the prep work of a listing. The house is bought in its current condition, so the roof, the AC and the yard stay as they are. Describe the property, receive an offer and name your closing date, and a title company handles the paperwork. Put the number beside a listing's likely result. Nothing requires you to accept.

For an inherited house or an owner who lives elsewhere, collect the deed or probate papers, the utility account details and contact information for whoever will sign. This keeps the title company from chasing paperwork and speeds up the date you can close.

faqs.q: How many people live in St. George, Utah?
faqs.a: The estimate is 108,713 for July 1, 2025, compared with 95,342 in the 2020 census. It is the largest city in Washington County.

faqs.q: When are St. George property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 every year. Later payments are delinquent and draw a 2.5% or $10 penalty, whichever is greater, cut to 1% when paid in full by January 31.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a St. George house sells?
faqs.a: The title company splits it at closing. You pay for the days you owned the house, and the buyer pays the rest. Any unpaid balance is cleared at or before closing.

faqs.q: Does St. George have special water or landscaping rules?
faqs.a: Yes. A 2022 water district ordinance limits grass at new homes and bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial and industrial sites, and a heavy-use fee started in 2023. Check with the city about your lot.

faqs.q: Can I sell a St. George house that needs repairs or has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. We take houses as they are, including those with old repairs, heat-damaged roofs or tenants. Describe the house and you will get an offer you can turn down.
